/-- `XReach` is closed under sequences of kernel steps (§57). -/
theorem XReach.kseq {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s s' : S3} (hr : XReach k statics s)
    (h : KSeq k s s') : XReach k statics s' := by
  induction h with
  | refl => exact hr
  | tail _ hs ih => exact .step ih (.kernel hs)

/-- The guarantee of §57 on the kernel side of library runs (HandlePool v0.4 annex): `KInv` on
every state reached by kernel steps O1–O16 and ends of slot contents. It is not a clause of the
contract and is not proved here: `xreach_inv` reduces it to the preservation of `KInv ∧ KAux` by
every kernel step, which the transfer of §63 breaks (`transfer_breaks_kinv`). -/
def KernelGuarantee (k : K) (statics : Statics) : Prop := ∀ s, XReach k statics s → KInv s

/-- A library step from a kernel state in `XReach` lands in `XReach`, under `KInv` (§57;
HandlePool v0.4 annex). -/
theorem xreach_pstep {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L L' : PState}
    (hr : XReach k statics L.kern) (hk : KInv L.kern) (hs : PStep k L L') :
    XReach k statics L'.kern := by
  rcases pstep_kernel hk hs with h | ⟨q, i, hpre, he⟩
  · exact hr.kseq h
  · rw [he]; exact .step hr (.contentEnd hpre)

/-- The kernel state of every library-reachable state is reached from `S3.init statics` by kernel
steps O1–O16 and ends of slot contents (§57; HandlePool v0.4 annex), given `KInv` on such
states. -/
theorem pReach_xreach {k : K} {statics : Statics} (hX : KernelGuarantee k statics)
    {L : PState} (h : PReach k statics L) : XReach k statics L.kern := by
  induction h with
  | init => exact .init
  | step _ hs ih => exact xreach_pstep ih (hX _ ih) hs

/-- `KInv ∧ KAux` (§57) holds on every state reached by kernel steps and ends of slot contents,
when it holds initially and every kernel step O1–O16 preserves it (`contentEnd_preserves` covers the
ends of slot contents; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3). -/
theorem xreach_inv {k : K} {statics : Statics}
    (h0 : KInv (S3.init statics) ∧ KAux (S3.init statics))
    (hK : ∀ s s', KInv s → KAux s → KStep k s s' → KInv s' ∧ KAux s') {s : S3}
    (h : XReach k statics s) : KInv s ∧ KAux s := by
  induction h with
  | init => exact h0
  | step _ hs ih =>
    cases hs with
    | kernel hs => exact hK _ _ ih.1 ih.2 hs
    | contentEnd hpre => exact contentEnd_preserves ih.1 ih.2 hpre

/-! ## Helper lemmas (lists, chains, effects) -/

/-- An optional value satisfying a predicate with default `False` exists (§38). -/
theorem optP_false_iff {α : Type} {o : Option α} {P : α → Prop} :
    OptP o P False ↔ ∃ y, o = some y ∧ P y := by
  cases o with
  | none => simp [OptP]
  | some y => simp [OptP]

/-- The replaced element belongs to the list (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: pool updates; §46). -/
theorem mem_set_self' {α : Type} : ∀ {l : List α} {i : Nat} {a x : α}, l[i]? = some a →
    x ∈ l.set i x
  | [], _, _, _, h => by simp at h
  | _ :: _, 0, _, _, _ => by simp
  | _ :: l, i + 1, a, x, h => by
    simp only [List.getElem?_cons_succ] at h
    simp only [List.set_cons_succ, List.mem_cons]; exact .inr (mem_set_self' h)

by steps from states satisfying `KInv`, the kernel state is reached by kernel steps and ends of slot
contents, and the ghost invariants hold. -/
theorem pReachI_inv {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState} (h : PReachI k statics L) :

steps from states satisfying `KInv` (HandlePool v0.4 annex). -/
theorem PReach.toI {k : K} {statics : Statics} (hX : KernelGuarantee k statics) {L : PState}

  induction h with
  | init => exact .init
  | step hr hs ih => exact .step (ih (pReach_xreach hX hr)) (hX _ (pReach_xreach hX hr)) hs

/-! ## `PoolInv` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4) -/

/-- `PoolInv`, item 1 (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4; non-normative library contract): the entries of
every pool lie in its storage and are pairwise disjoint (§40). -/
def EntriesDisjoint (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ pl ∈ L.pools,
    (∀ sl ∈ pl.slots, ∀ l ∈ footprint L.kern.P sl.place, l ∈ footprint L.kern.P pl.storage) ∧
    ∀ (a b : Nat) (sa sb : Slot), pl.slots[a]? = some sa → pl.slots[b]? = some sb → a ≠ b →
      ∀ l ∈ footprint L.kern.P sa.place, l ∉ footprint L.kern.P sb.place

/-- `PoolInv`, item 3, the transition guarantee (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4; non-normative library
contract): `freeSlot` never succeeds while an active descendant of a companion of the pool covers
the slot concerned (§43, §69). -/
def FreeGuarantee (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (L' : PState), FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L') →
    ∀ (pl : Pool) (sl : Slot), L.pools[j]? = some pl → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
      ∀ r ∈ L.res, r.pool = pl.id → ∀ x, L.kern.Active x → (x = r.comp ∨ r.comp ∈ L.kern.ancs x) →
        ∀ l ∈ L.kern.afp x, l ∉ footprint L.kern.P sl.place

/-- `PoolInv` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, as corrected; non-normative library contract): entry
disjointness, `pool_no_stale_access`, and the transition guarantee of `freeSlot` (§55, §57). -/
def PoolInv (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop := EntriesDisjoint L ∧ NoStale L ∧ FreeGuarantee k L

/-- `EntriesDisjoint` follows from the ghost well-formedness (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 1)
(§40). -/
theorem entriesDisjoint_of {L : PState} (hwf : PoolWF L) : EntriesDisjoint L := by
  intro pl hpl
  have hok := hwf.pools _ (List.mem_map_of_mem hpl)
  exact ⟨fun sl hsl l hl => hok.slotIn sl.place (List.mem_map_of_mem (f := (·.place)) hsl) l hl,
    fun a b sa sb ha hb hab => hok.disjoint a b sa.place sb.place
      (by simp [Pool.shape, ha]) (by simp [Pool.shape, hb]) hab⟩

/-- The transition guarantee follows from the ghost well-formedness (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4,
item 3): an active descendant of a companion of the pool is younger than `internal`, so it is
neither `internal` nor one of its ancestors, and `ContentEndPre` forbids it to cover the entry (§43,
§69). -/
theorem freeGuarantee_of {k : K} {L : PState} (hwf : PoolWF L) : FreeGuarantee k L := by
  intro j h L' hst pl sl hpj hsl r hr hrp x hx hxr l hl hlq
  cases hst with
  | @ok pl' sl' hpj' _ _ hsl' hpre =>
    rw [hpj] at hpj'; cases hpj'
    rw [hsl] at hsl'; cases hsl'
    obtain ⟨hint, hlt, -, -⟩ := res_internal hwf hr (List.mem_of_getElem? hpj) hrp
    obtain ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ := hx
    have hex := hpre.entry x (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy)) ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ ⟨l, hl, hlq⟩
    have hcx : r.comp ≤ x := by
      rcases hxr with rfl | hc
      · exact Nat.le_refl _
      · exact Nat.le_of_lt (chain_lt hc)
    unfold Exempt at hex
    rcases hex with rfl | h'
    · omega
    · have := chain_lt h'; omega

/-- `pool_inv_preserved` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4): `PoolInv` holds on every state of a library
run whose steps start from states satisfying `KInv` (§57); with `PReach.toI`, on every
library-reachable state under the guarantee of §57. -/
theorem pool_inv_preserved {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState} (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    PoolInv k L :=
  have ⟨_, hwf, hns, _⟩ := pReachI_inv h
  ⟨entriesDisjoint_of hwf, hns, freeGuarantee_of hwf⟩

/-- `pool_entries_disjoint` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 1; §40). -/
theorem pool_entries_disjoint {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState} (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    EntriesDisjoint L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved h).1

/-- `pool_no_stale_access` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 2): on every state of a library run
(`PReachI`), an active entry authority designates a live slot at its current generation (§89). -/
theorem pool_no_stale_access {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState} (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    NoStale L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved h).2.1

/-- `pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 3): on every state of a
library run (`PReachI`), `freeSlot` never succeeds while an active descendant of a companion of the
pool covers the slot (§43, §69). -/
theorem pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState}
    (h : PReachI k statics L) : FreeGuarantee k L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved h).2.2

/-- `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2: "La propriété d'exclusivité
concerne toutes les suites d'opérations admises du noyau"): on every state of a library run
(`PReachI`), whatever its kernel steps, an active `Modify` companion of a pool is its only active
companion (§43, §50). -/
theorem pool_resolve_modify_exclusive {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState}
    (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    ∀ r₁ ∈ L.res, ∀ r₂ ∈ L.res, r₁.pool = r₂.pool → L.kern.Active r₁.comp →
      L.kern.Active r₂.comp → r₁.mode = .modify → r₁.comp = r₂.comp := by
  intro r₁ hr₁ r₂ hr₂ hp ha₁ ha₂ hm
  refine Decidable.byContradiction fun hne => ?_
  have := (pReachI_inv h).2.2.2 r₁ hr₁ r₂ hr₂ hp hne ha₁ ha₂
  rw [hm] at this; cases this.1

/-- A handle of another pool is not valid (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2, D.3; §89). -/
theorem not_handleOK_other {pl : Pool} {h : Handle} (hid : h.id ≠ pl.id) : ¬ HandleOK pl h :=
  fun ⟨e, _⟩ => hid e

  fun ⟨_, ho⟩ => by rw [hsl] at ho; exact hg ho.1

## Observation (contract problem, not a module or kernel defect)

**O1. Ancestor exemption plus identity-only guard lets one pool end another pool's live slot.** Evidence: `pool_two_freeSlot_cross`, conjuncts 5–9.
- Pool 0 has `internal` 5, the root of storage 5. Pool 1 has `internal` 6 on the same storage. Authority 6 is derived `Modify` from 5 and held by leaf 4.
- §56 accepts pool 1, because distinct identities are not forbidden "merely because their footprints overlap".
- `freeSlot` of pool 1's slot 0 (place 6) is `ok`. The exemption of annex D.3 ("hors `internal` et ses ancêtres") covers both 6 and its ancestor 5. Place 6 goes from `Init` to `Uninit`.
- Place 6 is pool 0's slot 0, which is still `live` at generation 0 in pool 0's metadata.
- Safety is not at stake: pool 0 cannot resolve the slot while 6 is active (`ResolveStep … .reject`, §43 case 3), and later reads of the `Uninit` content are rejected (O9).
- Pool 0's abstraction contract is broken: a live slot loses its content without any operation of pool 0. §56 says it protects exactly this kind of consistency, but it keys only on identity.
- **To arbitrate:** either restrict the exemption to `internal` itself, or to ancestors not serving as `internal` of a live administration, or accept the behaviour.

content.content:
## 36. Shared Mutation and Internal Administration

An abstraction may keep its metadata in `SharedMutable` storage and modify it through `writeShared` to the extent permitted by the applicable rights and contracts. **Shared mutation of metadata does not, however, grant the right to create, recycle, or terminate exclusive authority over the administered storage.** Such operations require `internal` to be exercisable in `Modify` mode from the value administering the storage.

For every administrative abstraction, including arenas, `HandlePool`, and `DataStack`, **`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on the administering value**. The `writeShared` branch alone is insufficient. Operations issuing, recycling, ending, or invalidating regions must preserve active authorities and dependencies. Allocation through administration shared among simultaneous holders, under an interface not providing such exclusive exercise, cannot be expressed in safe code with only these sequential operations: any synchronized implementation of it belongs to Spec 2. These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel.

## 37. Dependent Values and Persistent References

When a value depends on the validity of other storage, that dependency must be carried by an explicit mechanism. In particular, this model retains:

- joint ownership or legal transfer of the resource;
- **non-escaping** dependent values, governed by `depend`, `store`, `AnchorOrder`, and end-of-use operations; they may survive a call if their anchors come from still-valid caller resources;
- library handles checked for identity and generation upon resolution, which are not authorities by themselves;
- validity durations bound to a frame or context, without a universal system of first-class lifetimes;
- safe abstractions encapsulating, when necessary, unsafe operations and proofs of their obligations.
----
## 56. Uniqueness of Live Administration

**An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction**, whether an arena, `HandlePool`, `DataStack`, or another library administrative instance. Before registering a new abstraction, its creation operation must jointly check the absence of that identity from **all relevant registries of live administrations**. Uniqueness concerns the identity of the `internal` authority, not merely possible overlap of footprints: abstractions with distinct `internal` identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap. Library contracts must make the information required for this guard available to the creation operation; checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient.

**This guard is not a condition for any safety property in Section 57.** The effective right (Section 43, case 3) already prohibits a second issuance over leaves covered by an active block derived from the same authority. Rather, the guard preserves the **abstraction contract**: without it, simultaneous administration of the same `internal` could cause `reject` instead of `fail`, or reissue a previously released block that the first administration still considers unavailable. It creates neither permissions nor allocations and introduces no general detection of authority cycles. Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel.

## 57. Main Invariant

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan
\]
----
## 89. Handles and Persistent References

In a generation-based pool library abstraction, a handle may contain a logical pool identity, an entry identifier, and a generation. This handle is not, by itself, an access right. Safe resolution temporarily supplies authority when the pool and entry are valid; a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure. These conditions belong to the safe abstraction's contract and do not modify the authority-discipline kernel.

## 90. Global and Called Frame

Global storage is anchored to the base frame, but a called function does not acquire ambient authority to modify it merely by being invoked. To access a global, it receives a derived authority under `enterFrame` conditions and may exercise only its effective modes.

| Name | Statement | Clause |
|---|---|---|
| `reachable_kinv_false` | `¬ ∀ k statics s, DDSound k → StaticsOK statics → Reachable k statics s → KInv s`. Witness: `transfer_breaks_kinv` extended by its transfer step; `StaticsOK cycStatics` is decided. | §57, §63 |
| `KStepDU` (def) | `∃ op, op.Step k s (.ok s') ∧ ∀ src dst, op = .transfer src dst → s'.Usable dst`. The docstring says it is a hypothesis on runs, not a clause of §63 or §57. | §57, §63 |
| `ReachableDU` (inductive) | closure of `KStepDU` from `S3.init statics` | §57 |
| `ReachableDU.reachable` | `ReachableDU ⊆ Reachable` | §57 |
| `kstepDU_iff` | `DDSound k → KInv s → KAux s → HeldAnchored s → (KStepDU k s s' ↔ KStep k s s' ∧ KInv s')` | §57, §63 |
| `reachableDU_kinv` | `DDSound k → StaticsOK statics → ReachableDU k statics s → KInv s ∧ KAux s ∧ HeldAnchored s`, with `KInv = WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan` | §57, §47 |

`kstepDU_iff` shows that the restriction is exactly "the step keeps §57". From a state where the
invariant holds, a kernel step is a `KStepDU` step iff its resulting state satisfies `KInv`. So,
by induction from `init_kinv`, `ReachableDU` is the set of states reached by runs along which §57
holds at every state. This run-level equivalence is not stated as a separate theorem.

### (c) Initial state

| Name | Statement | Clause |
|---|---|---|
| `init_kinv` | `StaticsOK statics → KInv (S3.init statics) ∧ KAux (S3.init statics) ∧ HeldAnchored (S3.init statics)` | §47, §49, §50–§54, §57 |

5. **§58 "only `alloc` may produce `fail`"** is stated over `KernelOp.Step`. "Leaving the state
   unchanged" holds by representation: `Outcome3.fail` carries no state. This is kernel-defs
   reading 47.
6. **`KAux` and `HeldAnchored`** are auxiliary invariants carried through the induction. Neither
   is a clause of §57. Both are discharged on the reachable states of `reachableDU_kinv`, whose
   conclusion contains `KInv` exactly.

## Problems found / for arbitration

- **P-M1 (= SP-A1 / P-T1, now at the level of §57).** §57 is false as stated
  (`reachable_kinv_false`). The witness satisfies both of §57's hypotheses, `DDSound` and
  well-formed statics. The exact repair, on states where the auxiliary invariants hold, is "the
  transfer destination is usable in the resulting state" (`transfer_kinv_iff`). This is the
  draft's dropped clause. Adding it to §63 as a precondition would make `reachableDU_kinv` the
  unconditional §57.
- **P-M2 (P-T2 resolved for these runs).** The §63.7 gap only matters on states without
  `HeldAnchored`. `HeldAnchored` is an invariant along every `KStepDU` run, so with the P-M1 repair
  §63.7 as written suffices.
- **§47 statics (P2, recorded).** `init_kinv` and `reachableDU_kinv` take `StaticsOK` as a
  hypothesis that §47 does not state. Review finding F2 notes that `StaticsOK` (`ShapeOK 0`) also
  requires owners to precede the statics they own. That is stronger than acyclicity, so it narrows
  the domain of the init theorems to declarations listed owner-first.

61:- **Defined failure:** a situation rejected at runtime with a specified consequence (for example, an error value or controlled termination).
65:**Safe code cannot cause any UB, regardless of which language rule is concerned.** A defined failure is not UB. Unspecified situations do not, by default, authorize UB in safe code: they must be explicitly resolved before normative stabilization.
73:Failure of a dynamic check in a safe interface must prevent the dangerous operation and result in a defined failure. An implementation may eliminate a semantically required check only if it demonstrates that the condition holds, without changing the permitted observable behaviors.
231:Violation of a safety obligation of an **unsafe raw** read constitutes UB. A safe read interface must establish the condition or report a defined failure before the dangerous operation.
250:Conditions 4, 5, and 6 are not concretely defined by this kernel; they remain explicit, parameterizable obligations. A raw write violating a safety obligation is UB; a safe interface must prevent it or produce a defined failure.
263:Successful deallocation ends the allocation's validity. Accesses carrying its provenance can no longer read or write that old storage. An attempted double deallocation through the raw operation violates a safety obligation and constitutes UB. A safe abstraction that detects an incompatible attempt before performing a dangerous operation may produce a defined failure; this does not require a universal checked-deallocation primitive.
307:Memory-machine relations may be deterministic and mathematically total even when certain obligations are not constructively decidable. A classical proof of totality is not a runtime requirement. Modeling a defined failure of resource reservation belongs to the allocator contract: it does not change the classification of violations of safety obligations of raw operations.
648:The following operations are abstract transition rules. They distinguish rejection by the discipline, defined failure, and a permitted transition.
658:`reject` means that the static discipline does not permit the step; it is neither an implicit runtime trap nor `ub` in the elementary memory machine. `fail` is a **defined failure** leaving the state unchanged; **only `alloc` may produce it in the O1–O16 kernel**. Other kernel operations produce `ok` or `reject`. Library-abstraction operations, including `issue` (§77), may define their own `fail` cases. Where such failure is provided, static preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract.
1043:In a generation-based pool library abstraction, a handle may contain a logical pool identity, an entry identifier, and a generation. This handle is not, by itself, an access right. Safe resolution temporarily supplies authority when the pool and entry are valid; a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure. These conditions belong to the safe abstraction's contract and do not modify the authority-discipline kernel.

/-- With the legal exercise of `internal`, an invalid handle makes `resolve` fail, and `fail` is its
only outcome (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2: "⇒ `fail`, sans changement d'état"; §58). -/
theorem pool_resolve_invalid_fails {L : PState} {j : Nat} {pl : Pool} {h : Handle} {m : Mode}
    (hp : L.pools[j]? = some pl) (hR : ResolveRight L.kern pl m) (hH : ¬ HandleOK pl h) :
    ResolveStep j h m L .fail ∧ ∀ o, ResolveStep j h m L o → o = .fail := by
  refine ⟨.fail hp hR hH, fun o ho => ?_⟩
  cases ho with
  | noPool hn => rw [hp] at hn; cases hn
  | noRight hp' hn => rw [hp] at hp'; cases hp'; exact absurd hR hn
  | fail => rfl
  | noEntry hp' _ hH' => rw [hp] at hp'; cases hp'; exact absurd hH' hH
  | ok hp' _ hH' => rw [hp] at hp'; cases hp'; exact absurd hH' hH

/-- `pool_resolve_stale_fails` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §89: "a stale identity or generation
leads to defined failure"). -/
theorem pool_resolve_stale_fails {L : PState} {j : Nat} {pl : Pool} {h : Handle} {m : Mode}
    {sl : Slot} (hp : L.pools[j]? = some pl) (hR : ResolveRight L.kern pl m)
    (hsl : pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl) (hg : sl.gen ≠ h.gen) :
    ResolveStep j h m L .fail ∧ ∀ o, ResolveStep j h m L o → o = .fail :=
  pool_resolve_invalid_fails hp hR (not_handleOK_stale hsl hg)

/-- `pool_resolve_other_pool_fails` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §89). -/
theorem pool_resolve_other_pool_fails {L : PState} {j : Nat} {pl : Pool} {h : Handle} {m : Mode}
    (hp : L.pools[j]? = some pl) (hR : ResolveRight L.kern pl m) (hid : h.id ≠ pl.id) :
    ResolveStep j h m L .fail ∧ ∀ o, ResolveStep j h m L o → o = .fail :=
  pool_resolve_invalid_fails hp hR (not_handleOK_other hid)

/-- With `AdminRight`, an invalid handle makes `freeSlot` fail, and `fail` is its only outcome
(HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "`fail` si l'identité ou la génération ne correspond pas; un slot déjà
libre n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité"; §58). -/
theorem pool_freeSlot_invalid_fails {k : K} {L : PState} {j : Nat} {pl : Pool} {h : Handle}
    (hp : L.pools[j]? = some pl) (hR : AdminRight L.kern pl) (hH : ¬ HandleOK pl h) :
    FreeSlotStep k j h L .fail ∧ ∀ o, FreeSlotStep k j h L o → o = .fail := by
  refine ⟨.fail hp hR hH, fun o ho => ?_⟩
  cases ho with
  | noPool hn => rw [hp] at hn; cases hn
  | noRight hp' hn => rw [hp] at hp'; cases hp'; exact absurd hR hn
  | fail => rfl
  | noEnd hp' _ hH' => rw [hp] at hp'; cases hp'; exact absurd hH' hH

/-- Decidability of `AdminRight` (§36; DS-v1). -/
instance (s : S3) (st : Stack) : Decidable (AdminRight s st) := by
  unfold AdminRight; infer_instance

/-! ## `newStack` and the guard of §56 -/

/-- The stack registry as a registry of live administrations (§56; DS-v1, non-normative): the
`internal` identities of its live stacks. -/
def stackInternals (s : S3) (stacks : List Stack) : List Nat :=
  (stacks.filter fun st => decide (s.Active st.internal)).map (·.internal)

/-- Preconditions of `newStack(storage, internal)` (DS-v1, non-normative; §56): those of `newArena`
other than its guard (`NewArenaBase`, §76.1–§76.3 and §76.5 read for a stack), and the guard of §56
over the stack registry and every other registry of live administrations `others`. -/
structure NewStackPre (s : S3) (stacks : List Stack) (others : List (List Nat))
    (storage internal : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- §76.1–§76.3, §76.5, read for a stack (DS-v1). -/
  base : NewArenaBase s storage internal
  /-- §56: no live administration of any registry uses `internal`. -/
  guard : Guard56 (stackInternals s stacks :: others) internal

/-- Decidability of `NewStackPre` (§56; DS-v1). -/
instance (s : S3) (stacks : List Stack) (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) :
    Decidable (NewStackPre s stacks others storage internal) :=
  decidable_of_iff (NewArenaBase s storage internal ∧
    Guard56 (stackInternals s stacks :: others) internal)
----

/-! ## `mark` (DS-v1) -/

/-- Metadata after `mark` (DS-v1, non-normative; library metadata, §36, §38): a mark naming stack
`j`, with the fresh identifier `fresh` and the current top, is appended to the live marks. -/
def markMeta (j : Nat) (st : Stack) (fresh : Nat) : Stack :=
  { st with marks := st.marks ++ [⟨j, fresh, st.top⟩] }

/-- `mark(j)` (DS-v1, non-normative; §58 outcomes; §36: metadata only, no right created): `ok`
on an existing stack; the identifier is fresh. -/
inductive MarkStep (j : Nat) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → MarkStep j D .reject
  | ok {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
      MarkStep j D (.ok ⟨D.kern, D.stacks.set j (markMeta j st D.fresh), D.fresh + 1⟩)

/-! ## `rewind` (DS-v1) -/
----
/-- `grow(j, b, extra)` (DS-v1, non-normative: in place only, using the derived `issue`): `reject`
when `b` is not a block of the stack or `extra` is zero (reading recorded); `release` of `b` (O3);
then the derived `issue` of Part XIV (`Arena.IssueD`) of the region of the same base and of size
`size + extra` into the recorded destination, on the released state: its static checks
(`IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2), `fail`, the state unchanged, unless the extension is in place
(DS-v1 "fail otherwise", availability §77.4), `split` of `internal` (O2) and `store` of the new
block (O8). -/
inductive GrowStep (k : K) (j b extra : Nat) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
  | noBlock {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = none →
      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
  | noExtra {st : Stack} {x : Blk} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x → extra = 0 →
      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
  | release {st : Stack} {x : Blk} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x → 0 < extra →
      ReleaseStep b D.kern .reject → GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
  | static {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x →
      0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
      ¬ IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst →
      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
  | fail {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x →
      0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst →
      ¬ InPlace st x extra → GrowStep k j b extra D .fail
  | split {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x →
      0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst → InPlace st x extra →
      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)] s₁ .reject →
      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
  | store {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ s₂ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x →
      0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst → InPlace st x extra →
      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)] s₁ (.ok s₂) →
      StoreStep s₁.A.length x.dst s₂ .reject → GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
  | ok {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ s₂ s₃ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x →
      0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst → InPlace st x extra →
      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)] s₁ (.ok s₂) →
      StoreStep s₁.A.length x.dst s₂ (.ok s₃) →
      GrowStep k j b extra D (.ok ⟨s₃, D.stacks.set j (growMeta st x extra s₁.A.length), D.fresh⟩)

verdicts.reason: Reproduced. FreeGuarantee (HandlePool.lean:1436-1443) has the conjunct `r.pool = pl.id`. Neither D.4(3) nor the brief has it. D.4(3) reads "freeSlot n'aboutit jamais si une descendante active d'une compagne couvre le slot concerné", and the brief says "an active companion descendant". In the nested-pool state x10, the guarantee holds only because of that filter: x10.res contains only a resolution of pool 0, and the freed slot belongs to pool 1. The cause is in the contract. D.3's exemption ("hors internal et ses ancêtres") also exempts a companion of another pool when that companion is an ancestor of `internal`. D.3's "En particulier, aucune descendante active d'une compagne ne doit subsister" is therefore false in this case. Nothing records the narrowing. readings/handlepool.md has no entry for it. reports/handlepool.md:66-68 describes the theorem as "a companion of the pool" but does not flag that this is narrower than D.4(3). Observation O1 in corpus-lib.md derives pool 1's internal from pool 0's internal, not from a companion. One of O1's proposed fixes ("ancestors not serving as internal of a live administration") would not fix this case, because 6 is a companion and not an internal. The theorem as stated is therefore weaker than the obligation it is claimed to discharge, and the literal obligation is false on a PReachI state. The exclusivity part (two_modify_companions) is weaker evidence: companion 9 is a reborrow descending from 6, and "les nouvelles compagnes" plausibly means companions of the same pool. The FreeGuarantee part alone supports major.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced. When a pool is dead (internal inactive), its registry entry is kept, and HandleOK checks only that the id matches and that the slot is live at the right generation. Every resolve on that pool therefore gives `reject`, and `reject` is the only outcome. The verdict is `reject` under H-R3 and also under H-R3's recorded alternative ("handle fail first"), because HandleOK pl4 ⟨0,0,0⟩ holds. H-R4 (missing pool index) does not apply, because the index still names the dead pool. So no recorded reading or alternative covers this case. By §58's terms, "defined failure" means `fail`, and §89 requires defined failure for a stale identity. D.1 ties staleness to destroyed pools ("détruire puis recréer ... ne réactive pas un ancien handle"; "Chaque pool vivant conserve une entrée abstraite"). pool_resolve_stale_fails cites §89 but assumes ResolveRight, which excludes this case. The conflict with §89 is therefore unrecorded. Treating a dead pool as a stale identity is itself a reading, so this is minor.

Spec §58 (line 658): "`fail` is a **defined failure**". §89 (line 1043): "a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure". verdicts.reason: Reproduced. On a PReachI state whose slot content is Init (written), freeSlot ends that content. Kernel endUse is rejected both for the slot place and for the storage root, and internal 3 stays active. Under the adopted readings (strict §69.2, kernel reading 28), no kernel sequence can reach that state while keeping internal. So the library run's kernel side leaves Reachable. corpus-lib.md:57 says so: "It is Reachable exactly when the run has no freeSlot". The fact is recorded, as "freeSlot is not a kernel endUse" in reports/handlepool.md "Contract problems". That record is presented as settled ("preservation of §57 proved"), and its witness, freeSlot_not_endUse on w4, only ends an Uninit slot.
